question: What does the Mahadevan/Parpola standardized text layer add to the M-2104 / Marshall no. 532 / 034 problem?
finding: M77 page 0084 confirms the Mahadevan text no. 2527 layer behind local id 2527.1, and Parpola 2019 confirms M-2104 as a standardized text no. 12 with UIII plus signs 15 and 1. This strengthens the explanation for the local crosswalk but downgrades it as raw evidence: Parpola explicitly says the actual shapes require CISI photos, the checked public layer still has no explicit M-2104 = no. 532 / VS 875 bridge, and Marshall's five-character description conflicts with the four-token local row. A follow-on CISI Vol. 2 Pakistan scope check corrected the next source target: that volume states its Mohenjo-daro section covers M-595 and M-621 to M-1659, so M-2104 must be sought in CISI 3.1/supplemental material or museum/archive metadata rather than CISI Vol. 2 Pakistan.
research_consequence: M-2104 remains a quarantined candidate source route, not an accepted 034 attestation. The useful progress is localization of the exact standardized-text layer where compression entered: M77 text no. 2527 / local 2527.1 / Parpola M-2104. A follow-on CISI Vol. 2 Pakistan scope check shows the next bridge should target CISI 3.1 or later supplemental Mohenjo-daro material, or museum/archive metadata, because CISI Vol. 2 Pakistan states its Mohenjo-daro coverage ends at M-1659.
